objective: Bind every simulation run's metadata, replay and verification to the registry scenario identity and to the evidence-policy and verifier-rule versions, so a run cannot be replayed or verified against the wrong scenario definition, and a missing or mismatched definition fails closed.
decision_supported: Whether a stored run can be attributed to the scenario definition that produced it, and whether replaying it with a different definition is refused rather than silently accepted.
acceptance: the same event stream under two scenario versions produces two different run identities, and the two differ only in the version that changed
run identity is a documented canonical serialization with a named hash algorithm over a fixed, ordered input list
replaying or verifying a bundle whose recorded metadata is absent, unknown, or mismatched against the registry fails closed with a stable diagnostic rather than falling back to a default scenario
the evidence-policy and verifier-rule versions are part of the identity, so changing either changes the identity
a run's recorded release_eligible status cannot be raised by omitting metadata, and a scripted fixture stays release_eligible false
identity computation is a pure function of its declared inputs, so two processes computing it from the same bundle agree
evidence: pytest transcript for tests/unit/test_run_identity.py with the passed count
check_run_identity.py stdout showing the identity of each committed run directory and exit code
the identity vector table: same events, two versions, two policy versions, four distinct identities
ruff check and ruff format output
stop_conditions: the change would require editing a frozen fixture, a seed, a scene hash or a committed matrix document
the change would require a contract amendment to libs/contracts or interfaces/, which needs three human approvals
the change would require adding a runtime dependency or importing ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt or a hardware SDK
the change would require a physical or Gazebo claim, which this repository cannot make from a fixture
the change would require reinterpreting an existing stored run directory rather than adding a field to it
data_classification: public repository source, documentation and test fixtures; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may write the identity module, the gate, the metadata wiring and the tests; a named human Owner accepts the identity input list and the hash algorithm
risks_and_fallbacks: the identity could omit an input that actually changes semantics; fallback is that the input list is a single ordered constant with its ordering asserted by a test, and any new input is an explicit addition that changes every identity by construction

an existing run directory without the new metadata would be unreadable; fallback is that a bundle with no recorded identity is reported as MISSING_IDENTITY with the fields it lacks, rather than being treated as a mismatch or silently accepted
the gate could pass vacuously when there are no run directories; fallback is that the gate reports the count it inspected and a test asserts the zero-run case is INCOMPLETE rather than PASS

the metadata extension could diverge from the registry reader; fallback is that the identity is computed from the registry entry the reader returns, and a test drives a real committed manifest through both
rollback is a revert of this commit; the module, the gate and the metadata fields are additive and no fixture, seed or scene hash changes
